_doc: Orientation ground truth for the Stage 00 resolver (tools/normalize). Each spread's correct UPRIGHT orientation, independent of the (spurious) EXIF tag. upright_aspect = required output aspect; raw_is_upright = the stored pixel buffer is ALREADY upright and any EXIF rotation is spurious (resolver must apply net 0 rotation, ignoring EXIF); exif_orientation = the tag actually present. All of this owner's phone captures share this spurious EXIF-on-upright-landscape pattern, so this file also guards that the resolver keeps the existing (OSD-rescued today) testset images upright. || 2026-08-18: entries carrying known_defect_applied_rotate document a rotation the resolver currently gets WRONG; the test asserts the defective value so that fixing the resolver trips a clear failure instead of passing silently.

de_01.note: German via-ferrata guide (Latemartuerme), sharpest of 3-frame set 1/2/1; spurious EXIF 6, figure-heavy so OSD conf ~0.04-1.46 fails today -> ingests sideways. THE orientation-break fixture.

de_02.note: German via-ferrata guide (Rotwand), sharpest of 3-frame set 1/2/2; spurious EXIF 8; same failure mode as de_01.

skewset_orient_01_134655.note: multi-view frame; upright is the PINNED per-set majority (0 deg CW). RESOLVER DISAGREED on this set: orientation OVERRIDE to majority 0deg; resolver disagreed on ['134655'] (low-conf OSD, see orient.py)
skewset_orient_01_134655.known_defect_note: THE RESOLVER GETS THIS WRONG TODAY, and that is why the frame is in the fixture. tools/normalize accepts an OSD 180-degree call at conf 2.58 / 3.09 because DEFAULT_MIN_OSD_CONF = 2.0, and layer 5's landscape prior cannot catch it: a spread rotated 180 degrees is still landscape. Correct upright is net-0 (raw_is_upright), so this entry asserts the DEFECTIVE value on purpose. When the resolver is fixed this assertion fails -- that failure is the signal to delete these two keys, not to loosen the test.
